label: first copy step echoing an e/f first token (rare, content-gated)
explanation: Sparse feature (about 0.01% of steps). About 85% of activation mass is at recall_idx==1, the step right after <DEL> where the input is the echoed first token and the model outputs original token 1. Within that step it fires almost only when the first token is e or f (j is a weaker third, about 4% of mass). The predicate recall_idx==1 & in_tok in {e,f} covers about 80% of activation mass, but precision is only about 2%: most such steps stay silent. Whether it fires depends on the rest of the sequence. Rate rises when original token 1 (the current output) is e, j, t or u, and when k (also b, m) appears in the sequence. It falls as the sequence has more digits, and longer sequences fire more often. Adding the out_tok and contains-k conditions raises precision to about 40% but drops recall to about 32%, so the gate looks like a diffuse sum of many token contributions rather than a clean conjunction. The largest activations, up to max 0.28, are f/e first tokens with k-heavy content. Weak residual activity (about 10% of mass) is in the original phase at late positions (t>=4) on assorted tokens, often in sequences that start with f. It does not fire at t<4, at the <DEL> step itself, or at later copy steps (recall_idx>=2).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=e (+4.13), orig3=k (+3.65), orig1=j (+3.32), orig0=j (+3.17), orig4=k (+2.83), orig2=k (+2.77). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.35), orig_idx=-1 (-2.00), orig2=x (-1.87), next_out=- (-1.71).
